beginner: can identify serif, sans-serif, monospace, display classifications
sets readable body copy (measure, leading, size)
working_professional: designs type systems with clear role assignment across breakpoints
controls measure (45-75 chars), leading (1.2-1.6x), and tracking intentionally
uses type scale with harmonic ratios (major third, perfect fourth, golden ratio)
understands optical sizing and variable font axes
designs tabular data, labels, annotations as first-class typography
senior: diagnoses readability failures causally (not just 'too small')
understands how typography interacts with composition, color, and motion
selects typefaces for product identity, not decoration
designs information hierarchy that survives responsive collapse
critiques density, scan patterns, and information architecture through typography
lead_director: establishes typographic voice that scales across products and media
knows when a type system needs character vs. when it needs restraint
approves typeface selection with accessibility, performance, and licensing awareness

type_system_principles.definition: Size, weight, case, color, position, and spacing differentiate information levels. Use at least 3 of these channels for robust hierarchy.
Line length (measure) of 45-75 characters for body text. Shorter for captions; can be longer for headings. Measure affects reading comfort as much as size.
type_system_principles.failure: measure-drift: body lines span full viewport width at desktop

type_system_principles.definition: Consistent baseline grid creates structural order. Line-height multiples align elements even when they span different type sizes.
type_system_principles.failure: rhythm-break: adjacent blocks float at different vertical offsets

type_system_principles.definition: Harmonic ratios (1.25 major third, 1.333 perfect fourth, 1.5 perfect fifth, 1.618 golden ratio) produce intentional contrast between levels.
type_system_principles.failure: arbitrary-scale: sizes chosen by eye with no mathematical relationship

type_system_principles.definition: Every typeface in a system has a role: body, heading, UI, data, code, display. Roles constrain usage and prevent ad-hoc font selection.
type_system_principles.failure: role-drift: heading font used for body, display font used for UI labels

type_system_principles.definition: Type designed for display sizes differs from type designed for text sizes. Optical size axes or separate optical variants ensure readability at every scale.
type_system_principles.failure: single-optical: display typeface used at 12px with collapsed stroke contrast

readability_principles.definition: WCAG 4.5:1 is minimum. Beyond ratio: font weight, size, anti-aliasing, and background complexity affect real-world readability.
readability_principles.failure: passes-ratio-fails-real: 4.5:1 but thin weight on photographic background unreadable

readability_principles.definition: Information density must match user task. Dense applications need tighter typography; editorial reading needs generous spacing.
readability_principles.failure: wrong-density: editorial at application density or dashboard at reading density

readability_principles.definition: Users scan before they read. F-pattern and Z-pattern scanning behavior should inform heading placement, bold lead-ins, and key information positioning.
readability_principles.failure: unscannable: walls of text with no entry points, bold terms, or structural breaks

information_design_principles.definition: Numbers in tables and data displays must be tabular (fixed-width) and right-aligned for magnitude comparison. Proportional figures destroy scan-ability.
information_design_principles.failure: proportional-data: proportional figures in data columns create jagged reads

information_design_principles.definition: Labels, captions, annotations, and metadata each need distinct typographic treatment. Not everything is body or heading.
information_design_principles.failure: label-flattening: all secondary text at same size/weight/color

information_design_principles.definition: Type scales, measure, and hierarchy must adapt to viewport. A 48px headline on desktop may need to become 32px on mobile — but relationship to body must survive.
information_design_principles.failure: scale-collapse: mobile headings and body collapse to same visual weight

failure_patterns.repair: cap body text containers at 65-75ch; test at every breakpoint
add at least 2 additional hierarchy channels
reduce to 2-3 typefaces with explicit roles, document in design system

causes: defaulting to system sans-serif without intention
failure_patterns.repair: select typeface(s) that express product character

symptoms: text readable on solid background, unreadable on image
causes: contrast tested only on flat backgrounds
failure_patterns.repair: test on photographic/video/gradient backgrounds, add text-shadow or scrim if needed
tabular figures, right-align numbers, consistent label treatment

why_is_my_type_hierarchy_weak: Are you using at least 3 channels (size, weight, color, position, case, spacing)?
Does your type scale use a harmonic ratio?
Is your heading/body contrast at least 2x in visual weight?
Does your hierarchy survive at mobile breakpoints?
why_is_my_text_hard_to_read: Is leading at least 1.4x for body text?
Is contrast at least 4.5:1 on actual backgrounds?
Is font weight at least 400 at the rendered size?
Are fonts loading before text is visible?

micro_labs.goal: Build a type scale from a chosen ratio, assign it to heading/body/UI/caption roles, and verify at 3 breakpoints
micro_labs.success: clear differentiation at every level, ratio consistent across breakpoints

micro_labs.goal: Design a typography system using exactly 2 typefaces (1 body, 1 display) with explicit role boundaries
micro_labs.success: no cross-role usage, every text element classifiable

micro_labs.goal: Test body text measure at 320, 768, 1024, and 1440px viewports; adjust containers until measure stays 45-75 chars everywhere
micro_labs.success: measure in range at all breakpoints

micro_labs.goal: Audit every text element on real backgrounds (not flat color swatches), record actual contrast ratios
micro_labs.success: all text elements meet 4.5:1 on actual backgrounds

transfer_tests.goal: Apply typographic principles from an editorial layout to a data-dense application UI
transfer_tests.success: hierarchy transfers, density adapts, identity survives

transfer_tests.goal: Swap typefaces while preserving all hierarchy, measure, and readability constraints
transfer_tests.success: hierarchy intact, new typeface expresses different character

golden_tasks.description: Audit a provided UI against all typographic dimensions: hierarchy, measure, contrast, roles, accessibility, responsive behavior
golden_tasks.evidence: structured audit with specific failure citations

golden_tasks.description: Given a typography system with identified failures, produce a repaired system with rationales
golden_tasks.evidence: before/after with role assignments, scale table, breakpoint behavior

golden_tasks.description: Test type scale survival across 4 breakpoints, diagnose collapse points
golden_tasks.evidence: breakpoint comparison table with specific hierarchy measurements

cross_pack_links.relationship: Typography is the structural material that gives composition its verbal dimension and frontend its information voice

version_sensitive_facts.fact: CSS text-wrap: balance and pretty support

known_limits: Typography quality depends on content context; this pack provides frameworks, not automated grading.
Font licensing must be verified per typeface selected.
Real readability requires human testing; automated metrics are necessary but insufficient.
provenance_note: Authored from model knowledge. Requires KAPIF research evidence before canon eligibility.
